title: CIA Director Ratcliffe makes unannounced Moscow trip
dek: CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow by military aircraft on Tuesday for undisclosed meetings with Russian officials. Neither Washington nor Moscow confirmed the nature of the visit or who he met. The trip is believed to be his first to Russia as CIA director.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: A U.S. military C-17 transport plane carried CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Moscow on Tuesday in an unannounced visit whose purpose and meeting participants remain undisclosed by both governments.
bottom_line: Watch for official statements from the U.S. State Department, CIA, or Russian Foreign Ministry disclosing the visit's purpose and participants. Any announcement regarding prisoner releases, detainee negotiations, or Ukraine peace talks would materially reshape the interpretation of this trip's significance.
body:
CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow on Tuesday by U.S. military aircraft for meetings with Russian officials whose nature and participants remain undisclosed, according to BBC News reporting based on flight tracking data and statements from unnamed officials.
A large C-17 transport plane departed Riga airport at 05:50 GMT and appeared to land in Moscow around 07:04 GMT, per FlightRadar24 data cited by BBC News. The aircraft returned to Riga shortly before 17:00 GMT. BBC News reports that neither Washington nor Moscow has confirmed who Ratcliffe was scheduled to meet or the purpose of the visit.
The trip is believed to be Ratcliffe's first journey to Russia as CIA director, though BBC News reports he has maintained contact with his intelligence counterparts in Moscow. In-person talks between high-level American and Russian officials are rare, BBC News states.
John Foreman, a British military attache to Moscow from 2019 to 2022, told BBC Radio 4's PM programme that such a high-ranking, unannounced visit at short notice typically signals that something significant is occurring. Foreman suggested the visit could focus on "escalation management" given recent drone activity speculation in Germany, or concern the release of U.S. detainees held in Russia, BBC News reports.
Ratcliffe played a role in negotiations for the release of Russian-American citizen Ksenia Karelina, who was jailed in Russia for over a year after being accused of providing support to Ukraine, according to BBC News. The CIA was involved in a 2024 prisoner swap with Russia that resulted in the release of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich, former U.S. Marine Paul Whelan, and Russian-American journalist Alsu Kurmasheva, BBC News reports.
The U.S. and Russia have maintained strained relations since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. President Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin at a summit in Alaska last year but the meeting did not produce a breakthrough, BBC News states. Subsequent U.S.-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to have stalled, according to BBC News reporting.
